name: This Month's Weekly Trail Maintenance
description:
Weekly Trail Maintenance
Dates to be determined, please email.
Leader: Wilfred
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com

Our club regularly helps with track and hut maintenance in our local area - a normal and important part of bushwalking club culture across Australia. Wilfred (and company) has been doing this work for decades, quietly giving back to the bush and the wider outdoor community through countless hours of volunteer effort.

These working bees are organised periodically, often weekly or even more frequently, depending on conditions and what needs doing. Tasks may include clearing vegetation, removing fallen branches, improving access, checking routes, and helping keep our local walking infrastructure usable and safer for everyone.

If you would like to lend a hand, learn a bit more about the tracks we use, or simply give back to the places we enjoy, get in touch with Wilfred for details. It is practical, meaningful work - and a good way to be part of the Club beyond the walk itself.

So, do you have what it takes to keep up with this old man?
Time to find out!

name: Sandals and Sundowners - Widowmaker Track, Castle Hill
description:
When: Friday 5 June 2026, 5:30 pm
Location: Castle Hill, Townsville
Leader: Luen
Grade: 3
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Join us for a relaxed Friday after-work wander up Castle Hill via the Widowmaker Track - with a small twist. Bring one drink in your pack, and we will enjoy a quiet sip together at the top before strolling back down to the cars (usually the road).

We will meet near the bottom of Castle Hill and make our way up the Widowmaker Track, one of the shorter but steeper walking routes on the hill. The climb is a good little workout, with rocky sections, uneven ground, and a few steeper pinches along the way, but we will take it at an easy, social pace with time to pause, catch our breath, and enjoy the afternoon light.

At the top, we will find a spot to take in the views over Townsville, enjoy a golden-hour drink together, and then descend via the road for a straightforward return. A head torch is recommended for the walk back down, as it may be getting dark by the time we return.

Bring:
- One drink of your choice
- Water
- Comfortable walking shoes with a good grip
- A head torch

A short climb, good company, and sunset over Townsville - not a bad way to end the week.

name: Shelly Cove Trail / Shelly Beach Trail
description:
Saturday 6 June 2026 - 6:30 am
Location: Cape Pallarenda Conservation Park / Townsville Town Common
Leader: Amanda
RSVP: ajdrill@gmail.com
Distance: Approx. 8 km
Grade: Easy to moderate
Walk type: Loop, with some beach walking

Join Amanda this Saturday morning for a relaxed coastal walk through the Cape Pallarenda and Townsville Town Common trail network, taking in the Shelly Cove / Shelly Beach area.

This walk follows a mix of formed tracks, coastal woodland, open country, and beach sections, with views across Cleveland Bay and towards Magnetic Island. Along the way, the group may pass WWII-era features, coastal scrub, mangroves, seasonal wetlands, and quieter sections of the shoreline.

The route is relatively flat, with only minor elevation gain, but walkers should still be prepared for soft sand, exposed sections, uneven surfaces, and warm conditions. Some of the tracks are shared with mountain bike riders, so please stay alert and give way where needed.

Please bring water, sun protection, insect repellent, suitable footwear, and snacks. As this walk includes coastal areas, please also be croc-wise and avoid entering the water.

RSVP to Amanda at ajdrill@gmail.com for meeting details.

description:

Location: Paluma Range National Park

Join Cherry for an adventurous overnight trip in Paluma Range National Park, using the DCK Shelter as a base camp. The group will walk in from Paluma Dam and spend the weekend exploring some of Paluma's rainforest tracks, creek systems, historic mining areas, rock gardens, lookouts, and waterfalls. Possible highlights include Crystal Falls, old mine sites, the Rock Garden, nearby lookouts, and, depending on the final route, Blue Lagoon and/or Junction Falls on the way out. The exact route is still being finalised, but the DCK Shelter has already been booked, so this trip is happening. Expect a classic Paluma weekend with rainforest walking, history, creek scenery, and good company.

name: Mt Stuart Road fitness walk
description:
Mt Stuart Road fitness walk - Tuesday mornings
Date: Tuesday 9th June 2026
When: Tuesdays, 4:45 am
Location: Mt Stuart Road, Townsville
Leaders: Wilfred
Grade: S15C
S = Duration: Short - under 4 hours
1 = Terrain: Formed track, fire trail, or very easy open terrain
5 = Fitness: Solid - good fitness needed for a full day out
C = Modifier: Climb - significant elevation gain or steep sustained ascent/descent
Short on time, but a steady 15 km bitumen climb to the summit and back. Terrain is easy; fitness demand is the main factor - but walk at your own pace.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com
The meeting location will be sent to those who RSVP.

Wilfred's regular Tuesday Mt Stuart road walk is open to club members who want a solid pre-dawn fitness hit. We will meet at 4:45 am and walk the bitumen road all the way to the 584 m summit and back, covering approximately 15 km return. This is a self-paced, steady uphill grind followed by a controlled descent - ideal for building endurance and leg strength. We walk up for 1.5 hours, which usually means we rest at the top and then go back down again ~1.5 hours.

As usual, we will bring a small bag and pick up rubbish along the way, giving the mountain a bit of care while we train. Bring water and a head torch, and be prepared for exposed conditions once the sun rises. No frills, just consistent effort, good company and sunrise views over Gurrumbilbarra.

name: Canyoning Overnighter
description:
When: Saturday 13 June to Sunday 14 June 2026
Location: To be decided
Leaders: Luen and Adrian
Grade: TBA - technical canyoning trip
Distance: TBA
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Join Luen and Adrian for a technical overnight canyoning trip on Saturday, 13 and Sunday, 14 June. The final location and route are still being decided and will depend on conditions, water levels, weather, access, and leader assessment closer to the date.

This will be an adventurous overnight trip involving canyoning, abseiling/rappelling, wet rock, slippery surfaces, steep terrain, creek travel, and movement in remote areas. Participants must have previous canyoning and/or abseiling experience and be comfortable wearing a harness and helmet for extended periods, following technical instructions, moving safely around cliffs and waterfalls, and carrying overnight gear.

This is not a beginner canyoning trip. Attendance will be at the leaders' discretion, and numbers may be limited depending on the route selected, group experience, and conditions. Participants should have a reasonable level of fitness, be confident in rough terrain, and be prepared for a full weekend outdoors in a remote environment.

Final details, including the location, meeting time, route, distance, grade, camping arrangements, and required gear, will be provided to approved participants after they RSVP.

Please bring appropriate gear for an overnight canyoning trip, including suitable footwear with good grip, food, water, overnight gear, dry bags, warm clothing, wet-weather gear, a wetsuit/sharkskin as it's cold, a head torch, and any personal technical gear as advised by the leaders.

Important: This trip is weather-dependent. Water levels, rainfall, access, and overall conditions will determine whether the trip goes ahead and which canyon or route is selected.

name: Castle Hill family scramble walk
description:
When: Sunday 14 June 2026
Location: Castle Hill, Townsville
Leader: Ryan
Grade: Family-friendly adventure walk, with steep and uneven sections
RSVP: ryan.toleman@gmail.com

Ryan will be leading a family-focused Castle Hill adventure for kids and parents keen to explore some of the hill's more interesting walking lines.

The planned route will likely head up via the Crack Track and return down the Ladies Track, giving the group a fun loop with a mix of steep walking, rocky terrain, scrambling, and great views over Townsville. The Crack Track is one of Castle Hill's more adventurous routes, with some hands-on sections and uneven footing, while the Ladies Track provides a more established and smoother descent.

This walk is intended as an introduction to adventurous bushwalking for families, rather than a fast-paced fitness hike. Kids aged 12 and over are welcome, but they must be supervised by a parent or guardian at all times. See our Child Protection and Risk Management Policy linked below. Participants should be comfortable walking on steep, rough, and rocky ground, and children should be confident moving over uneven terrain.

Bring
* At least 1 L of water per person
* Sturdy walking shoes with good grip
* Hat and sun protection
* A small snack
* Basic first aid

This walk is best suited to active kids and parents who are comfortable with short, steep climbs and a bit of scrambling. It may not be suitable for very young children, beginners with no bushwalking experience, or anyone uncomfortable with heights, loose rock, or uneven ground.

name: Walkers Creek
description:
When: Sunday 21 June 2026
Location: Walkers Creek, southern Mount Elliot range, Bowling Green Bay National Park
Leader: Molly and Cherry
Grade: M56
M = Duration: Medium - 4 to 6 hours
5 = Terrain: Sustained rough terrain, creek walking, boulder hopping, moderate scrub, some scrambling
6 = Fitness: Hard - sustained effort, steep climbing, or long rough travel
~6 hr off-track creek walk with long grass, rough creek travel, rock hopping, scrambling, swimming holes, and remote-feeling terrain.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
AWTGS=4/5 - off-track walking, long grass, creek travel, rock hopping, scrambling, and rough terrain
Distance: ~14 km return
Duration: Allow around 5-6 hours
RSVP: molly.hoey1@gmail.com

Join Molly and Cherry for a rewarding off-track walk to Walkers Creek, on the southern end of the Mount Elliot range in Bowling Green Bay National Park. This hidden creek system is home to granite creek scenery, swimming holes, small cascades, and the impressive single-drop Walker Falls.

Access for this walk is via private property and has been arranged with permission. Please do not attempt to access this area independently without landholder permission. Meeting details and access instructions will only be provided to those who RSVP.

The walk begins with cross-country hiking through long grass before reaching Walkers Creek. From there, the route follows the creek upstream, with plenty of rock-hopping, scrambling, and creek travel. There are several pools along the way, and depending on water levels, there may be opportunities to swim before continuing towards Walker Falls.

This is a reasonably strenuous walk, especially for those newer to off-track hiking, as the route is rough and mostly uphill on the way to the falls. Participants should be confident walking through long grass, moving over uneven rocks, scrambling around creek obstacles, and travelling in remote terrain where the easiest line may change as we go.

Bring:
- At least 2 L of water (recommended 3L)
- Lunch, morning tea, and snacks
- Sturdy footwear with good grip
- Sun protection
- Insect repellent
- Long sleeves and/or long pants for grass and vegetation
- Swimmers and a small towel if you would like to swim
- First aid kit with compression bandages

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP. Clicking "Going" on Facebook does not register you for the event. The meeting location and final details will be emailed to you by the walk leaders once you have RSVP'd.

name: The Ladies' Track, Castle Hill
description:
When: Friday 26 June 2026, 5:30 pm
Location: Castle Hill, Townsville
Leader: Jodie Rummer
Grade: S23C
S = Duration: Short - under 4 hours
2 = Terrain: Mostly track, or easy open country with minor uneven ground
3 = Fitness: Moderate - suitable for active walkers
C = Modifier: Climb - significant elevation gain or steep sustained ascent/descent
Short social climb on a formed historic track/stairs, descending by road. Fitness mainly from the short climb.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
AWTGS=3
RSVP: info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

Join us for a relaxed Friday after-work wander up the historic Ladies' Track on Castle Hill. This is a simple social walk to stretch the legs, enjoy the late-afternoon light, and take in the views over Townsville before strolling back down the road to the cars.

We will meet at the Cutheringa Trailhead lower car park and take the Ladies' Track up. The climb is around 2 km and takes roughly 30 minutes, following restored stone stairs, timber steps, and a contoured path cut into the hillside beneath the lower cliffs. This track traces a historic WWII-era route once used to access the Pill Boxes.

Suitable for beginners, it's a great way to meet some of the Club members and introduce yourself. Feel free to ask any questions you may have about the Club, upcoming walks, or places around Townsville. 

The pace will be easy and social, with time to pause, catch your breath, and enjoy the views. After reaching the top, we will descend via the road for a straightforward return.

Bring:
- Water
- Comfortable walking shoes
- A head torch, as it may be getting dark on the way down

A short climb, good company, and sunset over Townsville - not a bad way to end the week.

name: Alligator Creek area exploratory creek walk
description:
When: Saturday 27 June 2026, 7:00 am
Location: Alligator Creek area, Bowling Green Bay National Park
Leader: Luen
Grade: M55NW
M = Duration: Medium - 4 to 6 hours
5 = Terrain: Sustained rough terrain, creek walking, boulder hopping, moderate scrub, some scrambling
5 = Fitness: Solid - good fitness needed for a full day out
N = Modifier: Navigation critical - off-track route-finding or poor visibility of route
W = Modifier: Wet travel - swims, pack floats, frequent creek crossings, slippery rock, or prolonged water travel
Half-day exploratory off-track creek walk with rough ground, rock hopping, rainforest understory, and variable route choices.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
AWTGS=4/5 - off-track creek walking, rock hopping, and rough terrain
Distance: ~10km return
Duration: Half day, around 4-5 hours.
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Join us for a half-day exploratory walk in the Alligator Creek area of Bowling Green Bay National Park. The current plan is to explore one of the creeks in the area, with a mix of off-track walking, rock hopping, creek travel, and some contouring through the rainforest understory.

The exact trip plan is still being refined and will be reassessed closer to the date based on conditions, water levels, access, and the group's movement on the day. There are a few waterfalls and creek features we would like to investigate. They may be running low or even a little dry at this time of year, but the area should still make for an enjoyable morning of exploration, scrambling, and bushwalking.

Participants should be comfortable moving over uneven rocks, walking off-track, ducking through vegetation, and travelling in creek terrain where the easiest line may change as we go. This is not a long walk, but it will involve rough ground and some exploratory decision-making, so a reasonable level of fitness and confidence in off-track terrain is recommended.

Bring:
* At least 2 L of water
* Morning tea and snacks
* Sturdy footwear
* Sun protection
* Insect repellent
* Long sleeves or long pants for vegetation
* First aid kit and compression bandage
* A small dry bag or waterproofing for valuables

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP. Clicking "Going" on Facebook does not register you for the event. The meeting location and final details will be emailed to you by the walk leader once you have RSVP'd.

name: Paluma Winter Markets
description:
Come along to the Paluma Winter Markets on Sunday, 28 June 2026, from 9:00 am to 1:00 pm.

Enjoy a relaxed morning in the cool mountain air with fresh produce, plants, homemade preserves, baked goods, books, crafts, tea, coffee, cake, and a sausage sizzle.

This is a great chance to support the Paluma community, browse the stalls, catch up with locals, and enjoy a winter day trip up the range.

You can also make a weekend of it! Come up on Saturday for the Paluma Bush Dance at the Paluma Community Hall, then stay overnight and enjoy the Winter Markets on Sunday morning.

At this meeting, we will review key Club matters, discuss the year ahead, and consider items that affect membership, walk participation, and committee roles.

Example agenda items:
* Membership fee structure, including the proposed $40 annual membership fee.
* Whether visitor fees should be deducted from the membership fee when a visitor later joins the Club.
